doc.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Opening and why the Swing Era was popular
summary: Rowe introduces Best; they discuss why swing music was popular, with ballrooms and theaters full of dancers.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe, and we are filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive in San Diego, California, and I am very, very pleased to have Johnny Best, big band trumpeter and notable musician throughout many, many years of American music. Thank you so much for joining me today.
Well thank you for having me.
As I told you before the cameras were rolling, I have this idea that the big band days, that the Swing Era was a great time to be a young man. Was that a fair statement?
Well, people seemed to be pretty happy then, with that kind of music.
What was it about that kind of music that made it so popular?

That’s a hard one. Well basically it was dance music, and of course the country was full of ballrooms in those days, and people liked to dance. Ballroom dance. And I think that was, between the ballrooms and the theaters, that was what they liked.
